about.title: Reedley Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Reedley's mix of family-owned shops along I Street, grocery stores off Manning Avenue, and residential complexes near Dinuba Avenue means property owners have a duty to keep walkways, floors, and parking areas reasonably safe. When they fall short — a wet aisle left unmarked, a broken step, poor lighting in a stairwell — people get hurt. Under California law, a property owner or manager generally has to have known, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard before liability attaches, which makes the days right after a fall critical. Photos of the spill or defect, incident reports, and store surveillance footage often disappear fast if no one asks for them. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect Reedley residents hurt on someone else's property with an independent attorney who can start gathering that evidence, evaluate what happened, and explain your options — all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Reedley Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help pin down how long a spill, crack, or obstruction existed before your fall.

items.title: Fast Action Protects Evidence
items.desc: Surveillance footage at Reedley businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Connecting with an attorney quickly improves the odds that footage and incident reports get preserved before they're gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Shut You Out
items.desc: Even if a store argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule still lets you pursue partial compensation based on the other party's share of blame.

items.question: I fell at a store on Manning Avenue and didn't report it right away. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: Yes, though reporting sooner is always better for preserving evidence. You generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim against a private property owner in California. An attorney can help you reconstruct what happened even without an immediate incident report.

items.question: What if the property owner says I should have seen the hazard myself?
items.answer: That's a common defense, and it ties into California's comparative fault rules. Even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover compensation reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate how strong that argument really is in your case.

items.question: Does it matter that Reedley is a smaller city with fewer commercial properties than Fresno?
items.answer: Not for the legal standard — a Reedley grocery store, apartment complex, or agricultural business office owes the same duty of care as a larger property elsewhere in Fresno County. What matters more is documenting the hazard and getting witness or surveillance evidence before it's lost.
